title: Kanika Steels Pvt. Ltd. v. Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd.
coram: Sudhir Agarwal and Prabhat Chandra Tripathi, JJ.
disposition: Writ dismissed; additional-security and clause 4.20 challenges refused.
headnote: An industrial consumer’s writ to quash an additional-security bill, strike clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as inconsistent with section 47 of the Electricity Act, 2003, compel a pre-payment meter, and recover existing security with interest, was dismissed after the Court found no ground for any of the reliefs.
facts: Kanika Steels, an industrial consumer of Paschimanchal Vidyut Vitran Nigam Ltd., challenged a 1 October 2005 bill demanding additional security of Rs 2,99,062 and a Ministry of Power clarificatory letter of 11 February 2005. It sought to strike clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 as ultra vires the Electricity Act, 2003, a pre-payment meter under section 47(5) without security under the repealed law, and refund of Rs 5,16,661 already paid, with 12% interest under section 47(4). None appeared when the petition was called.

holding_units.holding: The Court, after perusing the record, found no ground to quash the additional-security demand, declare clause 4.20 of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 ultra vires the Electricity Act, 2003, compel a pre-payment meter under section 47(5), or refund existing security with interest under section 47(4). The writ was dismissed and any interim order vacated.
